To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) crowdturfers are organized into a hierarchical structure with a small number of professional workers at the top, (b) casual workers are recruited through middlemen, (c) the professional workers and middlemen have distinct characteristics from casual workers and regular social users, and (d) the hierarchical structure of the crowdturfers is reflected in the social networks of the workers in social media.
we identify three classes of social media crowdturfers, and we develop user models to automatically identify these crowdturfers.
we can automatically differentiate between crowdturfers and regular social media participants based on the properties of their tasks on crowdsourcing sites and their social media activities.

the results in the paper provide the first comprehensive study of the crowdturfing ecosystem, and the first attempt to identify crowdturfers and their activities on social media.

the results of our study are a step forward in understanding the structure and the nature of crowdturfing, and that the proposed methods and models are a step forward towards the development of tools that can be used to automatically detect and counteract crowdturfing activities.
